title: Nayanogor Somity — Cooperative Society & Microfinance Management System
shortDescription: A full-stack financial management platform designed to digitize members, savings, loans, DPS, collections, accounting, and reporting for cooperative societies.
overview:
Nayanogor Somity is a cooperative society and microfinance management platform built to replace manual paper and Excel-based operations with a centralized digital system.

The platform manages members, savings, loans, DPS, daily collections, accounting, financial reports, branches, and user permissions in one connected application.
challenge: Traditional cooperative societies often depend on paper ledgers and spreadsheets. Managing multiple financial transactions, loan repayments, guarantors, collections, and accounting manually can make reconciliation difficult and limit real-time visibility.
solution: I designed and developed a full-stack platform where business operations and accounting work together. Every major financial movement is processed through transactional workflows and reflected in a double-entry accounting ledger.
keyFeatures: Daily collection with multiple income heads
Financial reports with PDF & Excel export

engineeringHighlights.title: Double-Entry Accounting
engineeringHighlights.description: Every financial movement creates balanced debit and credit entries, keeping ledgers, cash books, and reports consistent.

engineeringHighlights.title: Transactional Integrity
engineeringHighlights.description: Financial operations such as collections, withdrawals, and loan disbursements are handled inside database transactions.

engineeringHighlights.title: Guarantor Validation
engineeringHighlights.description: Loan guarantor coverage is validated against the guarantors' live savings and DPS balances.

engineeringHighlights.title: Reporting Architecture
engineeringHighlights.description: Heavy reporting and ledger calculations are handled through PostgreSQL functions for efficient set-based processing.

learnings: This project strengthened my experience in financial system design, transactional database architecture, scalable reporting, and full-stack application development. It also reinforced the importance of treating accounting logic as a core part of the system rather than an additional reporting layer.
nextSteps: Expand automated testing for financial workflows
Move business rules into configurable settings
